Snovsk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Snovsk (formerly Korzhivka, renamed at the end of the 19th century) saw its earliest Jewish community established at the century's close, with formal settlement permission granted in 1882; Rabbi Shneur-Zalman Gorelik served the community in the early 1900s. Snovsk was the birthplace of three notable figures: Natan Rakhlin (born 1906), a Ukrainian conductor; Chaim-Shaul Bruk (born 1894), a rabbi who studied at the Lubavitch yeshiva Tomchei Tmimim and later led an underground Lubavitch yeshiva in Novohrad-Volynskyi, documented elsewhere in this collection; and Yehuda Slutsky (born 1915), a historian and writer. On November 4, 1941, 38 adult men were arrested and shot, with arrests continuing through December and January; the remaining Jewish population was shot in a nearby forest in January 1942. After the war, the remains of Jews killed in Snovsk and the surrounding county were relocated to this cemetery, where a monument was erected.
